# Plain-language interface copy

Status: InProgress

Apply the ISO 24495-1 plain-language principles to the launcher's catalog wording: a rule document, a review prompt with rewrite and cold-read passes, rewritten messages, and a guard that holds hints to one line.

## Scope

- In: docs/plain-language.md beside the design language
- In: The rewrite and cold-read prompt in the lumilio-i18n skill
- In: Rewriting zh-CN messages and the English written from them
- In: A catalog guard for hint length
- In: User guide sections that receive details moved out of a message
- Out: Game logs, content-source text and plugin-owned words
- Out: Other website and documentation pages
- Out: New UI surfaces for supplementary details, such as a link from the launcher to the guide; a message that needs one is listed for a separate decision
- Out: Reproducing the text of the standard

## Decision D1

Keep the rules in docs/plain-language.md, beside the design language.

Why: The Project Maintainer chose a separate document. Design language §8 keeps voice and form; the new document covers content and order.

Consequences: §8 links to it. A rule change updates the document in the same change.

## Decision D2

Cite ISO 24495-1 by clause and write the rules in our own words.

Why: The standard is copyrighted.

Consequences: The standard is not quoted or committed.

## Decision D3

Length limits come from the space of each place a message appears, and they are hard.

Why: A ⓘ hint is a tooltip that never wraps, so a long hint runs past the window. The standard measures plain language by whether readers can use the words, so fitting a limit is necessary but not sufficient.

Consequences: Facts that do not fit move to a key's own tooltip or the documentation. The cold read and screenshot review still decide whether a message works.

## Decision D4

Rewrite and evaluation run in separate agents: the rewrite pass may read the code, the cold read sees only the screen's words.

Why: An author who knows the mechanism writes it into the copy; a reader without that context shows what the words alone convey.

Consequences: Agents propose and do not edit. The main session applies changes after the Project Maintainer's review.

## Decision D5

Facts moved out of a message go to the user guide, except a fact needed to finish the action on that screen.

Why: The launcher has no link to the guide. What data goes to which service must stay findable [5.2.5], but the command variable names are needed to write a command.

Consequences: Translation services are on the content sources page and the diagnostics contents on a diagnostics page. The command dialogs keep a line of environment variable names, without $ or %, so it reads right on every system. A link from a message to the guide is a separate decision.

## Decision D6

A hint is named by its id: -help or -note. The guard measures messages by that name.

Why: The name is the one mark of where a message appears that a catalog test can read without parsing call sites.

Consequences: A ⓘ, a key's tooltip, a line under a field and an empty state's line use these endings. A new long hint fails the test; long-hints.txt only shrinks. Per-key tooltips replace an ⓘ that explains several keys (design language §9).

## Decision D7

Treat writing guidance as task-dependent defaults; consolidate voice in plain-language and retain the existing hint guard as an implementation constraint.

Why: In plan design-guidance, the Project Maintainer requested shorter design guidance that can adapt to feature needs.

Consequences: Supersedes D1's split of voice/content and D3's universal hard limits. D4's two-pass workflow becomes optional for ordinary edits. Existing test thresholds and first-batch acceptance remain unchanged; future work may change presentation and validation together when needed.

- Lesson: The first proposals kept 60–140 character help texts. The limits had been taken from the catalog's own length distribution, privacy text was allowed past them, and cold-read questions were answered by adding sentences. Settings help is a ⓘ tooltip that never wraps. Guard: plain-language §6 sets limits from each place's space, §3 and §7 stop questions from adding sentences, and hints_fit_one_line tests every hint.
